So I don't have a lot of money yet I want to buy some guns. Seems reasonable to me. Well to start things out you are limited to bolt guns. Not that his is a bad situation as all our special operations snipers are using bolt guns. I would also add that you can buy a couple of good bolt guns new for the price of a new black rifle. There is also the added advantage with two rifles you can hunt anything on the North American Continent from badgers to Brownies. Since low cost also equates to simple basic components we need to follow that cow path. There are really only two calibers that fill the bill when having only simple basic uncomplicated rifles. One is the .243 Winchester (NO I DO NOT OWN ONE) and the other is the .308 Winchester. Of course the purests will point out that the .243 in nothing more than a necked down .308 and they are right. But in that defense you can buy .243 and .308 ammo at any gun shop. Also if you can buy a RCBS reloading set up for about $180 so you can make your own .243 from once fired .308 but I digress.

With the .243 you can take varmints, and animals up to 350 lb body weight with no problem. That is most of the Antelope, Mule Deer and White tail in the country. I suppose you could throw in Texas Hogs and Black Bear in that category. The .243 with light projectiles is deadly on rabbits, prairie Dogs, rock chucks, Coyotes, and any other pests. Lightly loaded it is also enjoyable to shoot for an after noon at the range.

With the .308 Winchester you can move up to the bigger animals such as Wapiti and brown bear. You can also drop down to a 150 grain projectile for deer and antelope. So for about 800 you can have two excellent rifles, with associated reloading equipment and be set up for what ever comes, (plus the little woman ain't going to make you sleep on the couch.) Hell with the light recoil of the .243 she might even join you in the field for your next taking game trip, and I won't even go anywhere near doing IT in two sleeping bags zipped together!
